classes.title: Executor runs loop on an exhausted context
classes.summary: A conversation's executor runs failed on context exhaustion several times in a row. The engine retires a session that runs out, so each launch should run on another session: with `session_continued` false, none of them fit its model's context, and the brief or the window is the likelier cause; with it true, a session that ran out was continued anyway.

classes.title: A seat's turns fail in a row at one place in the engine
classes.summary: A seat's turns failed in a row at the same function, or a message on its inbox was lost to such a failure, for a cause the engine could not attribute to a provider, a credential, a budget, a box or its environment. The report names the function the failure left the engine's code through; a report at this class's own site means no function on the way out recorded it yet.

classes.title: A seat's message was dead-lettered
classes.summary: A message on a seat's inbox used up its whole delivery budget on hand-backs, the deliveries the engine returned to the queue rather than ran, while no node was draining and every node ran one build, and was moved to the dead-letter subject. The person or system that sent it was not answered. The report names why its last delivery was handed back.

classes.title: The engine panicked
classes.summary: A panic was recovered where the engine contains one, and the `scope` says in what: a turn, a tool call, a queue handler, a seat's loop, an API request. A panic is a defect in the engine rather than in anything it talks to. The report names the function that panicked and up to five of the engine's own frames under it, each a function, its file in the public source and a line; the panic's value stays on the node's log.

classes.title: The engine crashed
classes.summary: The engine's process ended on a crash the Go runtime could not recover from, and the node's next start found its output. The `fatal_kind` says what it was: a panic nothing recovered, a map used by two goroutines at once, a lock or a wait group misused, a stack past its limit, a native library's fault, every goroutine asleep, or another fatal error. A host out of memory or threads is never reported. The report names the engine function on top of the crashing goroutine and up to five of its frames; the rest of the output is deleted on the node, unsent.

classes.title: A schema migration failed
classes.summary: A numbered schema migration of a tagged release failed on a node's database, and the node reported it on its next successful start. The site is the migration file; `from_migration` is the last file the database had applied, so the two numbers reproduce the upgrade, and `sql_error_class` is the driver's class of refusal. The data that made it fail never leaves the node.

classes.title: An executor run was stranded by the engine
classes.summary: An executor's run ended with no turn able to resume it, for a reason the engine documents as an invariant of its own and not as its environment or a person's act: the run's record held none of its turn's parked state, its turn suspended with no conversation recorded, every attempt to resume a finished job failed on an error the engine could not attribute elsewhere, or its parked state was saved in a format an upgrade retired. The `reason` says which.
